sections.label: Audit Act amendment for follow-the-dollar audits
sections.summary: The Audit Act will be amended to let the AG conduct follow-the-dollar audits on non-government entities receiving public funds.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (on behalf of the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Audit Act will thus be amended to allow the AG to conduct "follow-the-dollar" audits on any non-government entities that receive public funds.

sections.label: Scope of audits under Bill
sections.summary: Audits under this Bill are limited to whether entities' use of public funds follows the funding agency's terms and conditions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (on behalf of the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The audits under this Bill are limited in scope to only whether the entities' use of public funds is in accordance with the terms and conditions specified by the Government agency that provided the funds.

sections.label: Minister for Finance public interest condition
sections.summary: The AG will conduct a follow-the-dollar audit only if the Minister for Finance is satisfied it is in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (on behalf of the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The AG will only be called upon to undertake the "follow-the-dollar" audit if the Minister for Finance is satisfied that it is in the public interest to do so.

sections.label: AG powers to obtain documents
sections.summary: The Audit Act will be amended to give the AG powers to search and obtain documents or information needed for follow-the-dollar audits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (on behalf of the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Audit Act will, therefore, be amended to provide the AG with additional powers to search and obtain all necessary documents or information which he requires to conduct a "follow-the-dollar" audit.

sections.label: Support for Audit Act changes
sections.summary: Current law leaves some publicly funded entities unauditable, so the Audit Act is updated to let the AGO audit them and obtain necessary documents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under current law, some of the entities that receive such public funding are not accessible for audit by the public auditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, there is the need to equip AGO with the powers to audit the non-government entities and to ensure that public funds are, indeed, properly used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The current laws, therefore, need to be updated to keep up with the times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I support the changes to the Audit Act which allow the AGO to conduct "follow-the-dollar" audit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The amendments would also enhance the powers of the AGO to obtain documents, information, records or equipment which are necessary to establish the proper use of the fund against its public intent and to ensure full accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hopefully, a balance can be struck with the provision under section 4A where the Finance Minister's approval must be sought on the basis of public interest to carry out the "follow-the-dollar" audit and for the Minister to set limits on the scope of the audit.

sections.label: New section 6A self-incrimination privilege
sections.summary: New section 6A states an individual cannot rely on common law privilege against self-incrimination to refuse providing required explanations, information, documents, records or answers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 6A states that an individual cannot rely on the common law privilege against self-incrimination to refuse to provide an explanation, information, document, record or answer a question required under section 6.

sections.label: Common law self-incrimination privilege
sections.summary: The clause makes explicit that a person cannot rely on the common law privilege against self-incrimination to refuse documents, information or questions from the AG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The insertion of this clause is to make explicit what is already in practice, that a person cannot rely on the common law privilege against self-incrimination to refuse to give documents or information or to answer questions from the AG.

sections.label: AG reporting to enforcement agencies
sections.summary: Where information shows a more egregious matter than an audit breach, the AG may report it to the Police or other enforcement agencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In situations where the information provided contains evidence of a more egregious matter than an audit breach, the AG may report and bring the matter to the Police or other relevant enforcement agencies.
